title: finding(app-shell): element:definition-list designer items write label/value while the renderer reads term/description — every designer-built list renders blank terms and em-dashes
body:
Found by the census objectui#8216 asked for (branch `claude/issue-8216-block-config-schema-parity`). Filed unassigned, out of that card's scope. Measured on `origin/main` `f20e57d62`.

## What

The page designer's `element:definition-list` item editors write `label` and `description`'s two keys under names the renderer does not read.

Producer — `BLOCK_CONFIG['element:definition-list']` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-config.ts`):

```
{ name: 'items', kind: 'array', itemFields: [
    { name: 'label', kind: 'text' },
    { name: 'value', kind: 'text' },
] }
```

`PageBlockInspector.renderField` writes an item key VERBATIM (`next[i] = { ...itemObj, [n]: v }`), so an author fills `items[i].label` and `items[i].value`.

Consumer — `DefinitionListRenderer` (`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/data-list.tsx:36`-`:70`):

```
interface DefinitionItem { term: string; description?: unknown }
...
DT renders {it.term}
DD renders {toText(it.description)}
```

and `toText` returns the em-dash `—` for `null` / `undefined` / empty string.

The block's own registry declaration agrees with the RENDERER, not with the designer — `ComponentRegistry.register('definition-list', …)` at `data-list.tsx:75` declares `items` as "Term/description pairs [{ term, description }]".

## Consequence, and why it is not a cosmetic mismatch

Every definition list built in the page designer renders an EMPTY term cell and a literal `—` for every row, no matter what the author typed. Both authored strings are still in the document; nothing reads them, and nothing says so. The list is not empty either — `items.length` is non-zero, so the renderer's own "No details" empty state never appears; the author gets a grid of blank labels and dashes and no diagnostic anywhere.

This is the shape AGENTS.md #0.1 exists for, pointing at the PRODUCER: the designer table's own file header states the rule it broke — "Keep each field `name` aligned with the property name the corresponding renderer reads."

## Why objectui#8216's gate does not catch it

`element:definition-list` is one of three `BLOCK_CONFIG` blocks that resolve to no runtime-judgeable schema on either face — it is absent from `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ComponentPropsMap` (it is not a spec `PageComponentType`) and absent from the `@object-ui/types/zod` node registry. objectui#8216's gate therefore carries it as an explicit exemption, which is exactly why this defect had to be found by reading rather than by the gate.

## The decision this needs

Rename the two item controls to `term` and `description`. It is not a one-line edit, and that is why it is a card:

- the field `name` is the last segment of the i18n key, so `engine.inspector.pageBlock.field.element:definition-list.items.label` and `...items.value` become `...items.term` and `...items.description` in BOTH locale tables in `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, and the retired pair must leave both (the pattern objectui#3829 and objectui#5212 set);
- documents saved by every released build carry the old spelling nested inside `items[]`, so the read-door question objectui#7772 answered with `stripRetiredBlockProps` applies — except this one is NESTED, which that helper does not reach;
- ⚠️ `label` is a plausible spelling for a term and a maintainer may prefer moving the RENDERER instead. That is a contract decision, not a spelling preference, and AGENTS.md #0.1 pushes it toward the producer; either way it should be decided once and written down.

## Related

objectui#8216 (the census that found it) · objectui#5212 / objectui#3829 (two earlier BLOCK_CONFIG keys that outlived their contract) · objectui#7772 (the read-door pattern for a retired designer key)
